record_notes.DCP-LETT-1482: May17, supplied1852 one-page ALS. Two retained blocks and bibliographic footnote. Catalogue and latest Journal requested to Athenaeum, not already received or read. May1851 catalogue correction date and1852 publication distinct from exact access; no surviving institutional incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1782A: November18, conjectured1855 from watermark and inferred award task. Three blocks and three footnotes. Text transcribed from Maggs catalogue of underlying two-page ALS, not inspected manuscript or guaranteed full original. Reluctant promise to send paper at very end of week, trip and engagements prospective. Westwood citation and old March nomination speech identification supplied/inferred in apparatus; body does not name Westwood or secretary. Could be Sharpey or Stokes, not certain named questioner. Later November30 award and printed citation not current completed work.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1425F: May1851 memorial from sale catalogue, four-page original described incomplete. Two retained blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. P1 is bracketed catalogue synopsis interspersed with short quotations, P2 is collective memorial excerpt between ellipses. Darwin is one of many listed signatories, individual drafting not established. Not a complete letter or individually attributable Darwin answer despite sender metadata. Appeal for Hooker employment, later1852annuity outcome separate. Signatory list, catalogue date and uninspected manuscript extent preserved; London supplied.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13892: Incomplete one-page Darwin ALS, questioned recipient Sharpey from provenance and questioned1853–72 broad tenure date. Two blocks and two footnotes. Opening conditional reference to unnamed man/list lost; Hooker to enquire after proposal before asking about attendance. Do not settle ambiguous pronouns as Hooker himself the proposed man; apparatus explicitly leaves other man/purpose unknown, while summary suggests Hooker. No exact date, Royal Society appointment identity or missing note recoverable. Window crosses Origin boundary; hold for date and recipient.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1800: December25, supplied1855, four-page ALS to conjectured Shaw from provenance. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Earlier suggestions led to introductions and letters already written; method of those suggestions unspecified, not necessarily a lost letter. Brand approach still conditional on skinning availability and acquaintance; no Angola specimens received. Claims written each chief world quarter except Arabia, seeks Aden contact. Erdhardt letter already written, Sykes assistance offered not performed. Apparatus Rev.S.Erhardt versus body Rev.J.Erdhardt discrepancy retained; do not merge automatically. Later1868 citation not current receipt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1703: June25,1855 damaged four-page Salter ALS. Seven blocks, four footnotes, separate Darwin annotations and bibliography. Missing Darwin letter acknowledged; experiments discontinued before earlier1852paper, not ongoing new controlled crosses. Geum hybrid abundant and precisely same as first crop, contrasting editorial summary great variability. Parent G.rivale foreign-pollen necessity only idea, not proved. Epilobium tracked through fourth year, later spontaneous seedlings could be second or later generation; not continuous numbered-generation certainty. Ripe seed/capsules promised, not received. Reciprocal Linaria cross hypothetical untried; damaged lines and Darwin-added mature retained separately. Apparatus infinite-generation generalization not established by this letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1438F: July4, supplied1851 incomplete four-page AL, mourning-border dating. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Darwin personally received Smith letter three days ago, derivedJuly1 under supplied year, but earlier Athenaeum postal arrival unknown. Letter dated the8th with month unstated; June is plausible inference, not explicit incoming date. Glacial versus iceberg argument remains contested; own Chiloe observations and possible tidal streams/eddies analogies, not proof identical Jura transport. Twelve missing lines, excised signature and postscript retained, not reconstructed from earlier book. Asks firsthand Jura examination and distinguishes coast-ice from true icebergs.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1767: October20, supplied1855 one-page ALS. Three blocks and two footnotes. Declines name insertion because no longer collects/works on an insect order, confirms missing slip correct. Apparatus addresses list of British entomologists with addresses; summary masthead unsupported. Later1856 omission separate from current request. Statement does not preclude all later insect-related correspondence or change taxonomic interests beyond its stated scope.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13844: July30, supplied1852 one-page ALS. Single block, no footnotes. Declines August3 Chevening invitation because house guests present; invitation known but source absent. Does not imply illness, disinterest in science, attendance or exact arrival of invitation. Personal invitation response eligible Darwin grounding in principle.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1579A: August22,1854 four-page letter to Mrs Stutchbury, not husband Samuel in Australia. Single long retained block, two footnotes and bibliography. Collection work finished; two or three large boxes still undetermined, directions requested and carriage-to-station planned. Proposes recipient pay carriage then report cost for reimbursement via postal order; do not read as immediate remittance or completed dispatch. Could add species, second-volume copy promised when completed; September distribution and actual later presentation not current possession.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1148: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. January 28, supplied 1848. Asks loan and destructive sectioning permission for Portuguese fossils after reading Smith paper. Collections already available from other men do not prove Smith specimens received. Discrimination by shell/internal anatomy uncertain for fossil genera. Requests geographic/habitat data and recent material. Malta-road interpretation admired as land-level/denudation evidence; later taxonomic treatment belongs apparatus. Monograph duration is forecast.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1153F: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. February 6, supplied 1848 by relation to January request. Missing Smith letter known, thanks gift of fossil Balani and Landsborough collection request. Fossils expected to be found at Geological Society on next London visit: thanks is not personal receipt. Future British Museum donation after work completion and spring arrival remain prospective; 1854 actual donation in footnote is not current outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1650: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Additional fresh full ALS March19,1855, three blocks, footnote and bibliography. Formal favorable referee recommendation for Horner valuable observations with future value forecast. P3 explicitly Figure3 not sent, so report does not prove receipt/examination of entire visual apparatus. Contrasts private criticisms in1649 without fabricating a preserved incoming manuscript conversation. Metadata routes to Sharpey/RoyalSociety; body authorship Darwin.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
